title: Crucial SSD not detected by BIOS or OS
shortDescription: Drive doesn't appear in boot menu or Windows.
fullDescription: Crucial MX500 (SATA) and T700 (PCIe 5.0 NVMe) detection issues typically trace to cabling, M.2 slot config, or firmware quirks. Check BIOS first – if not there, it's hardware or physical.

fixSteps.title: Reseat drive
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, reseat the M.2 or SATA SSD.

fixSteps.title: Update BIOS
fixSteps.instruction: For T700, ensure BIOS supports PCIe 5.0 x4; update to latest.

fixSteps.title: Test in another system
fixSteps.instruction: Rule out motherboard slot by testing in second PC.

faq.a: For full speed yes; backwards compatible with PCIe 4.0 at reduced speed.

title: TRIM disabled on Crucial SSD
fullDescription: Crucial Storage Executive reports TRIM status. Issue usually external enclosure, RAID array, or OS setting.

fixSteps.title: Check status
fixSteps.instruction: Run 'fsutil behavior query DisableDeleteNotify' – 0 means TRIM enabled.

fixSteps.title: Switch to AHCI
fixSteps.instruction: Change BIOS from RAID to AHCI (may require reinstall).

faq.a: Some RAID configs do; Intel RST-enabled AHCI passes it.

title: Crucial T700 throttling under load
shortDescription: Sustained writes cap far below rated speed.
fullDescription: T700 can exceed 12 GB/s reads, but generates significant heat. Without the Crucial or third-party heatsink, throttling kicks in within seconds of heavy load.
symptoms: PCIe link reported as Gen3 instead of Gen5

fixSteps.title: Install heatsink
fixSteps.instruction: Use Crucial's heatsink version of T700 or add motherboard M.2 heatsink.

fixSteps.title: Verify PCIe gen
fixSteps.instruction: BIOS/Storage Executive – confirm Gen5 link if board supports it.

fixSteps.title: Improve airflow
fixSteps.instruction: Case fans aimed at M.2 area.

faq.a: Yes – heat output requires active cooling for sustained speeds.

title: Crucial SSD firmware update
fullDescription: MX500 had firmware updates addressing unexpected wear counter bug. Always update firmware via Storage Executive before deploying.

fixSteps.title: Storage Executive update
fixSteps.instruction: Run Crucial Storage Executive > Firmware Updates.

fixSteps.title: Bootable ISO
fixSteps.instruction: If Windows update fails, use Crucial bootable ISO.

faq.a: Earlier firmware had unreliable SMART; later firmware stabilized.

title: Crucial SSD SMART critical warning
shortDescription: SMART indicates critical condition – failure near.
fullDescription: Storage Executive displays critical warning when wear, spare blocks, or errors exceed threshold. Back up immediately, plan replacement.

fixSteps.title: Inspect attributes
fixSteps.instruction: Identify which SMART attribute failed for RMA evidence.

whenToCallPro: Data recovery if backup can't finish.

faq.a: Percentage of remaining endurance based on writes and wear.

title: Crucial T700 overheating
shortDescription: SSD temperature exceeds safe operating range.
fullDescription: PCIe 5.0 drives like T700 run significantly hotter than Gen4. Without heatsink and good airflow, temps spike past 80°C under load causing throttling or protective shutdown.

fixSteps.title: Heatsink version
fixSteps.instruction: Buy T700 w/ heatsink or install motherboard M.2 heatsink.

fixSteps.title: Case fans
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure top/side fans blow across M.2.

fixSteps.title: Move M.2 slot
fixSteps.instruction: If CPU M.2 slot under GPU, move to secondary slot if thermal better.

faq.q: Can I use T700 without heatsink?

title: Crucial SSD bad blocks rising
fullDescription: Normal at low rates; rapid increase signals wear-out or defective NAND. Back up and plan replacement or RMA.
symptoms: Storage Executive reports bad block growth

fixSteps.title: Firmware update
fixSteps.instruction: Update firmware to confirm not a software bug.

faq.q: How many bad blocks are normal?
faq.a: A few over lifetime; rapid growth is not.

title: Crucial SSD became read-only
fullDescription: When rated TBW exceeded or serious errors encountered, Crucial SSDs may lock to read-only to protect data. Back up and retire.

fixSteps.title: Firmware update
fixSteps.instruction: Try firmware update – may clear if false positive.

faq.a: End-of-life read-only is permanent; firmware bug read-only may clear after update.
